# Multi-Level Work Breakdown Structure (WBS)

> **Ancillary design document**. This document is ancillary to
> [RFC-039 Compiler Architecture Restructuring](../../rfc/accepted/039-compiler-architecture.md). It
> expands RFC-039’s phase sequence into **independently committable and independently verifiable**
> tasks at three levels.
>
> RFC-039’s body is the sole authority for phase ordering and acceptance gates. This document is
> responsible only for breaking the work down to executable granularity and registering conflicts
> that remain undecided.

## Positioning and Scope

| Level       | Count       | Meaning                                                                                      |
| ----------- | ----------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **Level 1** | 11 (P0–P10) | Phases, corresponding one-to-one with RFC-039’s phase sequence                               |
| **Level 2** | 73          | Task groups: work groups decomposed by phase; each can be staffed and archived independently |
| **Level 3** | 262         | Work units that can be committed and verified independently                                  |

**Reserved numbers (not reused)**: P4 has no `4.7`/`4.8`, and P8 has no `8.1`; after the LALRPOP
route was withdrawn, `8.4` / `8.5` / `8.6` were also left unused (2026-11-25). No corresponding
entries for any of these have existed since the WBS was established: throughout the history of this
document, the three headings `**4.7` / `**4.8` / `**8.1` have had zero matches
(`git log -S'**4.7' -- docs/src/dev/architecture/09-execution-wbs.md` can verify this), and there
are no repository-wide references either. `8.1` corresponds precisely to Phase 1 of `05` (test
resurrection and completion): that phase was split into P1 (`1.1`–`1.3`) and `8.8`, so P8’s
numbering is aligned with its phase number (Phase 0 → `8.0`, Phase 2 → `8.2`, and so forth).

**Covered by this document**: task decomposition, dependency relationships, parallelization groups,
and binding of acceptance criteria.

**Not covered by this document**: the design rationale for tasks (see `02`–`08`) or the rationale
for phase ordering (see RFC-039).

**Registration convention (effective 2026-10-12)**: newly registered Level 2/Level 3 entries **must
include two fields**—“**Belonging phase**” (the P phase to which the task truly belongs, which may
differ from the containing section) and “**Blocks the mainline**.” `Pending scheduling` is no longer
the default state; an unmarked entry is considered **not schedulable**. Numbers must be **unique
across the entire document** (tasks on other tracks use a track number, such as `029g.x`, and must
not occupy `N.x`).

**Closure registration convention (effective 2026-11-24)**: checked entries contain only four
items—the task ID, status, **short implementation commit hash** (7 characters), and issue number, if
any—on one line:
`- [x] **3.24.1 Remaining pattern-matching completion work** ✅ 4d608df3 (issue #405)`. **Do not
write the fix, the criteria chain, gate thresholds, file line numbers, test names, or review
conclusions**: those belong in the commit message (`git show <short-hash>`). This table is a kanban
board, not a process chronicle. **Do not write adjudication labels or restate conclusions**: “User
adjudication A/B/C,” “Option A,” “Final implementation is…” and similar text do not belong in this
table. The board answers only “Is it complete?”; adjudications and results are found in commit
messages and RFC-039’s decision register.

**Short hashes are authoritative only after pushing**: closure entries record the short hash on
`origin/dev` after the push, in this order: **push the implementation commit first, then write the
closure entry** (see [commit-convention](../commit-convention.md), “Take the commit number after
push”). The closure commit itself carries no number—a self-reference is impossible.

**Count columns contain only numbers**: the Level 1/2/3 counts under `Positioning and Scope` contain
only current values; change history such as `+1 = …` does not belong in the table.

## Current State: Gaps Found During Decomposition

While consolidating the “Implementation Points” from eight documents into this table, **five hard
gaps in the documentation system itself** were found. All have now been closed:

| #   | Gap                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          | Resolution                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| --- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| G1  | **P5 has no implementation steps whatsoever**. RFC-039 defines P5 (checker splitting) and its acceptance criterion (C1 zero-diff), but none of the seven documents describes how to perform the split. `01-routing.md` mentions `annotations.rs` only in its directory tree—the sole mention in the entire batch.                                                                                                                                            | P5’s steps are supplied by this document (see below).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| G2  | **The three ownership assignments for the `include!` refactor resulted in no implementation**. RFC-039 lists it under P4; `02` assigns the cross-reference to itself; `06` also lists it under S7. However, `02`’s change list (6 additions + 20 modifications) contains **no `semantic_tokens.rs`**.                                                                                                                                                        | Implementation steps are assigned to §P5 5.1 of this document (after P4 is complete); references in RFC-039 and `06` now point here.                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| G3  | **Three overlapping inventories of CI scripts coexist**. RFC-039 lists four `scripts/ci/*.py`; `01` lists four scripts + 1 `cargo test`; `07` separately lists four checks (all with different names); `04` also previously listed `check-synth-boundary.py` (that script was cancelled by the user on 2026-11-24). After deduplication, there are **at least 9 new scripts and no canonical inventory**; `check-obligations.py` is owned by both P4 and P9. | See §P9 of this document for the canonical inventory (10 active scripts, each owned by one phase); all other documents refer to this table.                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| G4  | **Conflict over the fate of `precedence_inline.rs`**. `06` counts it among the “1005 lines requiring resurrection,” while B6 in the same document says it “must be deleted together with the `Precedence` enum”; `05` advocates deletion.                                                                                                                                                                                                                    | **Resurrect in P1, retain in P8** (decision record C1; Pratt is no longer to be deleted).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| G5  | **Conflicting descriptions of the L2 objective**. RFC-039 and this directory’s index say “grammar-driven syntax,” but `05` self-assesses: “**It did not adopt true grammar-driven parsing (LALRPOP); it only achieved a declarative lookup table.**”                                                                                                                                                                                                         | Converged on a **declarative precedence table + an unambiguous language surface**: the full LALRPOP grammar-driven route was withdrawn (the two attempts had 29 / 148 conflicts). Following 05:648, the fallback is “retain Pratt + a single declarative precedence table + cross-validation of two `BinOp` sources”; see P8 8.3. |

## Target Design: Phase Sequence

```
P0 仓库维护机制与代码放置规程 08 ← 新增，先立规矩
P1 复活孤儿测试并修缺陷 06 §S1
P2 建立等价性判据基线 07 全部
P3 修正确性漏洞（最小方案） 02 §S3-漏洞半部
P4 阶段契约与统一 Driver 02
P5 checker 文件内拆分 02 + 本文补齐
P6 类型表示单一化 03
P7 中间表示 SSA 化 04 } 可并行
P8 前端范式变更 05 }
P9 防反弹门禁（含统一脚本清单） 01 §防反弹 + 08 §可机检规则
P10 其余清理与状态修正 06 §S2/S3/S4/S5/S6
```

**Rationale for adding P0**: the three prohibitions (do not invent constructs / do not fill
indefinitely / do not patch what should be refactored) constrain every action in P1–P10. The rules
must be established before work begins; otherwise, while resurrecting tests in P1, work has already
started adding `mod` declarations to `tests/mod.rs`—precisely the cause of the G4 conflict.

### P3 Fix Correctness Vulnerabilities (Minimal Solution)

Source: [02](02-stage-contract.md) §Implementation Points S3, vulnerability-fix half + **2026-10-07
silent-discard-point audit (3.4)**

> **Semantic-correction routing (D59, adjudicated 2026-10-11)**: if this track or a later phase
> discovers a defect where the “old behavior did not count as success”—**A silent failure / B silent
> mismatch / C undefined behavior and resource loss** (crash, stack exhaustion, silently returning a
> wrong answer)—it **may be fixed along the way**, but all four requirements must be met: ① red
> first, then green (the red criterion must exist first and genuinely fail); ② do not change the
> externally observable behavior of programs that “previously compiled successfully and ran
> correctly” (must not turn success into failure, and must not remove or alter existing diagnostic
> codes/text/exit codes); ③ register in the same commit (this row identifies the error type + that
> phase’s revision note + the PR required block’s “Error Type” line); ④ regenerate the baseline in
> the same commit + manually review the diff. **D user-visible semantics / E external-contract
> tables / F RFC-level design changes still require prior adjudication. For the expanded criteria
> and A–F allowlist, see [07 §Semantic-correction routing criteria](07-equivalence-oracle.md); **the
> “default super-refactor + retroactive registration” approach is not adopted** (rationale: RFC-039
> D59: without a red criterion, fixes cannot be distinguished from regressions, conflicting with “no
> C5′” and “no relaxation whatsoever”).

**Acceptance**: vulnerability criteria turn green, and **deliberately removing the fix must turn
them red again**. **Risk**: adding E4018 to multi-file paths is a breaking change.

**3.4 acceptance**: 3.4.1 / 3.4.2 must have red criteria first (changing code first is forbidden);
3.4.3 is a manual review; 3.4.4–3.4.8 are governed by C2/C3 and P9’s 9.2 gate. **Risk**: the new
diagnostic in 3.4.1 is a behavioral change and requires synchronized corpus differential baseline
and CHANGELOG updates.

> **Stop-the-bleeding path**: P3 does not have to wait for all of P2. The only hard prerequisites
> for 3.1/3.2 are **2.3.2 (multi-file corpus layer) + 2.4.1/2.4.3 (two red criteria)**;
> 2.1/2.2/2.3.1/2.3.3 (IR verifier, snapshots, single-file differential testing, performance
> baseline) can proceed in parallel with P3. Stopping the bleeding from correctness vulnerabilities
> (such as `Sorted(3)` passing silently) must not be blocked by snapshot-infrastructure
> construction. 3.3 (panic-to-diagnostic conversion) has no prerequisites and can land at any time.

### External Track RFC-029g: Remove `pub` and Automatic Binding (External Track / #399 — Ordering Constraint D56)

Source: [RFC-029g](../../rfc/accepted/029g-remove-pub-and-auto-bind.md) (accepted 2026-10-02,
implementation not started) and [#399](https://github.com/ChenXu233/YaoXiang/issues/399). **This
track is not a design item of the refactor itself; it is a specification-compliance deletion forced
as a prerequisite by an ordering constraint**; it is distinct from P10 S5’s “reduce the visibility
of `pub` items” (narrowing Rust visibility to `pub(crate)`).

**Why it must be completed as a whole before P4**: RFC-029g’s deletion surface overlaps with the
rewrite surfaces of all four refactoring phases; reverse ordering means repeating the same deletions
and baseline updates on the new grammar / new checker layout / new SSA IR.

| ------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `KwPub` and syntax branches                                         | `lexer/{tokens,state,mod}.rs`; `parser/parser_state.rs`, `statements/{declarations,imports,functions,bindings}.rs` | **P8** (8.2 lexical convergence / 8.3 Pratt precedence convergence / 8.7 splitting `parse_assign_after_target`)                                                                                                                                                         |
| AST `is_pub` ×2 (`Assign` / `TypeDefinition`)                       | `parser/ast.rs`                                                                                                    | **P6 6.5 dead AST variants** + P8 + D1 directory renaming (`parser/ast.rs` → top-level `src/ast/`)                                                                                                                                                                      |
| `auto_bind_to_type` and the `pub` branch of `collect_exports`       | `typecheck/checker.rs`, `environment.rs`                                                                           | **P5** (the `include!`→real `mod` conversion and checker split are a **pure move**, and the `pub` branch will be moved verbatim into the new files)                                                                                                                     |
| Dead-code exemptions `exempt_pub` / `is_exported` and role dispatch | `typecheck/passes/dead_code.rs`, `module/orchestrator.rs` (inside `check_project`)                                 | **P4 4.2.2** (`check_project` slimming)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| `Public` modifier in `semantic_tokens`                              | `typecheck/checker/semantic_tokens.rs`                                                                             | **P4 4.2.6** + P5 + 4.6 (D55)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| `is_pub` ignored binding in `ir_gen`                                | `middle/core/ir_gen.rs`                                                                                            | **P7** (SSA-ization of `ir_gen.rs`)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| 31 occurrences of `pub` in `src/std/`                               | `std/list.yx` / `json.yx` / `option.yx` / `result.yx`                                                              | No phase changes them directly, but **P6’s hard acceptance criterion requires no diff in `src/std/` (`git diff --stat src/std/` is empty; directly driven tests under `tests/` are exempt, as described in P6’s hard-acceptance section)**—they can only land before P6 |

**Incidental benefit**: RFC-029g removes the dead `env.exports` table (written by the producer and
never consumed anywhere in the repository) and the `is_exported`/`is_visible` accessors ⇒ P4’s 4.3
obligation ledger loses one more “produced but never consumed” field.

**Acceptance (behavioral changes, red criterion first)**:

1. **Red first, then green**: each of the two behavioral changes must first land a red criterion
   before code is changed—① `pub` changes from “silently accepted” to a parse error; ② unreferenced
   top-level bindings in Lib/Script roles now report W1001 (previously `pub` items were absolutely
   exempt).
2. **Test count must not decrease**: when deleting the `exempt_pub` case and `is_pub` fixture in
   `typecheck/passes/tests/dead_code.rs`, equivalent new cases must replace them.
3. **Baseline in the same commit**: diagnostic-set changes (new parse error + new W1001) ⇒ update
   the corpus differential baseline (`tests/baselines/corpus-parity.jsonl`) and CHANGELOG in the
   same commit; IR snapshots are expected to have zero diff, and any non-zero diff must be
   explained.
4. **Independent revert unit**: the entire batch occupies one commit group and must not be mixed
   with other phases (DoD 6).
5. `cargo test` / `clippy -D warnings` / `python scripts/rfc/check_tracking.py` are all green.

**Ordering**: overlaps with 3.4 files (`checker.rs`, `environment.rs`) ⇒ the two must be serial and
cannot run in parallel; **the whole track precedes P4** (RFC-039 D56). RFC-029g does not depend on
3.4; the implementer chooses which to start based on the context at hand.

> **Commit correspondence (2026-10-08)**: the adoption of this section (the P3.5 chapter +
> main-chain/constraint row) and RFC-039’s D56 were both incorporated into `97071c81b` while the
> parallel-flow sweep cleaned the workspace—the commit message records “3.4 additional
> registration + D57/D58 adjudication filing” and does not mention this track. History is not
> rewritten; following the existing convention (the `d5b18390` precedent, see the P2 landing note),
> the change is registered in place as retrospective bisection evidence.

|                                            | 4.9.9 A cross-unit single-definition method called with a **named argument** loses its formal-name table (registered 2026-11-25, discovered during 7c closure): calling a cross-unit (registry-injected) method with a named argument reports `E1014 Function '…' has no parameter named '…' (available: )`—the name table is empty; positional calls to the same method work normally, as do named-argument calls within a single file. Minimal reproduction: `lib.yx` defines `Point.scale_by: (self: &Point, k: Float) -> Float`, and `main.yx` has `p.scale_by(k = 2.0)` ⇒ E1014, while `p.scale_by(2.0)` ⇒ 6.0. **D59 classification: Class C** (the old behavior was unsuccessful: the named-argument path silently dropped arguments and then failed at runtime or silently returned a wrong value; the positional path does not consume the name table and its behavior is unchanged. The mechanism is a **consumer-side key mismatch**—the IR-generation-side formal-name query has only three sources: the current unit’s `fn_param_names` / leaf name / module export surface; the first segment of the method key `{Type}.{method}` is a type name rather than a module key and therefore never hits the export surface). **Root cause and fix (single point, without introducing a second name table)**: ① `AstToIrGenerator::lookup_param_info` (`src/middle/lower/query.rs`) gains a `method_param_info` source—retrieve the formal-name table by `{module}.{Type}.{method}[#N]` from the existing unique cross-unit carrier `ModuleInfo::method_overloads` (candidate ↔ mangled name ↔ formal name as three parallel vectors; `extract_module_info` ← `method_overload_snapshot`, the same source as the typecheck injection surface), and the call site (`src/middle/lower/expr/call.rs`) uses the definition-unit qualified name from `method_dispatch_name` as the lookup key; ② the candidate-injection surface’s narrowing rule pairs by target (the defining-side type name), while alias-imported candidates are injected normally; ③ **provider priority** (a bare-name provider with `local == target` takes priority; aliases fill in only when no bare-name provider exists; same-level multiple modules with the same full name are skipped) is now a **shared single point**, `frontend::module::import_face::TypeCandidateProviders`—the injection surface (`driver::arms.rs`) and consumer side (`middle::lower::query`) read the same data and no longer evolve independently; ④ the **same-source criterion** (`method_source_mismatch`, `src/middle/lower/query.rs`): let `winner` = the providing module selected by the candidate-injection surface and `owner` = the receiver’s module (the same ownership determination used by `method_dispatch_name`)—`owner == winner` ⇒ allow (typecheck and IR use candidates from the same module; this is the bare-name positional-argument case, measured 2.0 + 2.0 = 4.0); `owner != winner` ⇒ allow only if both modules have **exactly identical candidate signatures** for the key (candidate selection does not affect type checking; the value is determined by the receiver’s owning unit—the existing behavior for cross-unit same-named types introduced through inline aliases), otherwise reject loudly (the existing E1107). **Positional arguments with identical signatures are still allowed** (4.9.8 fixture 0/0; the value is determined by the receiver’s owning unit). **Named arguments** are still always rejected loudly when the name itself is ambiguous (same-named type provided by ≥2 modules) (the shared criterion’s empty-table exit = the existing E1014): the name-table source is untrustworthy and cannot be checked by name; ⑤ **fallback for “do not silently discard named arguments”**: `reject_named_args_without_param_names` reuses the shared criterion `arg_binding::bind_args_to_params`’s empty-table exit (the existing E1014, with the same `available` semantics = an empty string), and is connected to the four IR-side arms that “have named arguments but cannot obtain the formal-name table”—the RFC-004 binding arm, namespace arm, ordinary method arm without overload resolution, and ordinary **static** function arm; built-in container construction (`src/middle/lower/expr/container.rs`) similarly rejects named arguments other than `len`; ⑥ **fallback exclusion is determined by binding identity**: closure-value bindings (`stmt.rs`’s `closure_fn_names`: the bound value is written as an `=>` lambda and the declaration has no value parameters), current-unit top-level function bindings (`declared_fn_names`), and **named nested function declarations** (`nested_functions` entries) all **do not enter** the fallback—all three have the old behavior “compile succeeds and named arguments are ignored,” and changing that to a compile-time error is D59 Class D; all three are registered as known gaps (D60 ② “should report but does not,” Class A). **Visible changes (list individually; do not merge into “no behavioral change”)**: ① cross-unit method named arguments (bare import / alias import / two overload candidates) change from an E1014 empty table to name-based slot binding (measured 6.0 / 30); ② aliased-import method named arguments change from silently dropping arguments (runtime `E6007`) to name-based slot binding (6.0); ③ named arguments on g9g generic curried methods change from silently dropping arguments (`b.v` reads Void, runtime `E6007 Void vs Int`) to compile-time E1014 (Class C); ④ cross-unit ordinary-function named arguments change from silently dropping arguments to E1014 (Class C); ⑤ named arguments on const-generic receiver methods change from silently dropping arguments to E1014 (Class C; the same **positional** shape still fails, an existing independent defect not covered by this task); ⑥ built-in container construction `Vec(Int)(foo = 3)` silently ignores the argument → E1014 (Class C; `Vec(Int)(len = 3)` remains 0/0 and has a value assertion `v.length == 3`); ⑦ whole-module imports (`use lib` + `lib.Circle(...)`) change from silently dropping named arguments to E1014 (Class C); ⑧ named arguments on a **name-layer ambiguous type** always produce E1014; positional arguments follow the same-source criterion: `owner == winner` and “`owner != winner` but candidate signatures are identical” are allowed (value assertions 4.0 / 200 / 20), while differing signatures produce E1107 (three measured silent-wrong-value cases are eliminated: differing formal types ⇒ 111 rather than 2.0, differing arity ⇒ 300 rather than 7, differing return types ⇒ 200 rather than 2.0); ⑨ closure-value bindings (top-level `f = () => 7` and those inside function bodies), block-body function declarations (`f: (a: Int) -> Int = { 7 }`), and named nested function declarations (body ignores formal parameters) **retain the old behavior** for named arguments (ignored; measured result 7), with no judgment change. **Residual / known gaps**: named arguments on those three declaration surfaces are still silently ignored (Class A, D60 ② “should report but does not”); named nested functions’ formal-name table is not yet connected to `lookup_param_info`; `E1014` text limitation: an empty `available` means “IR did not obtain the name table,” not “the function truly has no such parameter”; this change does not alter the text or broaden the diagnostic surface; same-source signature comparison is structural equivalence (it does not compare implementations), and the residual risk of “identical signature, different implementation” is covered by 4.9.10. **Criteria**: 19 driver-level direct cases in `src/driver/tests/named_args_cross_unit_method.rs` (cross-unit named arguments / alias import / overload candidate selection by name / table-driven multiple columns / whole-module import / RFC-004 binding / mixed-import named argument E1014 + bare-name-side positional argument 0/0 (4.0) + alias-side formal type/arity/return type, three E1107 cases + alias-side same-name formal E1014 / two bare-name providers, E5006 / top-level closure old behavior Int(7) / closure inside a function, old behavior / named nested function ignoring formal parameters, old behavior Int(7) / container-construction rejection + `len` value assertion / **invariant criteria**: the ambiguous shape must be red for named arguments + positional arguments with identical signatures are 0/0 and dispatch to the receiver’s owning module (200 / 20)), unit guards in `src/middle/lower/tests/query.rs` (an empty name table ⇒ `None`; deleting the guard makes it red), and project-level fixtures `tests/yaoxiang-multifile/named-args-cross-unit-method{,-alias-overload}`. **Completion revision**: first fix `02ed42d2`, fallback and `method_param_info` hardening `091b835b`, mixed-import provider priority and container rejection `5edfb53e`, review round (name-layer ambiguity rejection / closure-value identity / top-level closure / value assertions) `7e96a844`, and this round’s same-source criterion and shared provider table = the commit to which this row belongs (the short hash will be added by the closure commit). **Regression surface**: zero IR-snapshot drift, corpus parity 405 cases (all existing 403 cases byte-for-byte unchanged + 2 new fixtures), and 4.9.8’s 6 dispatch criteria remain green. | 4.9.7         | Criteria are in `src/driver/tests/named_args_cross_unit_method.rs` and this row’s “Criteria”; the boundary list is in the left cell under “Visible changes / Residual”; the root fix is in 4.9.10                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
|                                            | 4.9.10 Cross-unit method identity is undefined (registered 2026-11-25; structural issue confirmed during 4.9.9 implementation): the method-candidate key `{Type}.{method}` does not include module qualification. For same-named types across modules, three consumers—candidate injection (`arms.rs::visible_method_overloads`), typecheck’s formal-name/candidate matching, and IR dispatch (`method_dispatch_name`)—each **guess the provider by name**, so any change merely moves the “silent wrong value” elsewhere. 4.9.9 applies stopgap measure A (ambiguity ⇒ all method calls on that type are rejected loudly); the root fix = upgrade method keys to **module-qualified identity**, produce them from one resolver, and make all three consumers read-only, requiring changes to the `overload_resolutions` key shape and mangled names (D59 **Class D**, requires adjudication) ### P5 In-File Checker Split — Supplied by This Document (Original Gap G1)

Source: RFC definition + `01-routing.md` directory tree + hard constraint (the `pub(crate)` path of
`collect_used_in_type` must not change)

- [x] **5.1 `include!` → real `mod`** (2 Level 3 tasks)
- [x] **5.2 Extract `refinement`** (2 Level 3 tasks)
- [x] **5.3 Extract `annotations`** (2 Level 3 tasks)

| Level 2                     | Level 3                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                | Prerequisite | Acceptance                                                                                                                                        |
| --------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| 5.1 `include!` → real `mod` | 5.1.1 Change the `include!` at the end of `checker.rs` to a real `mod` declaration (the line anchor is not hard-coded; it was measured at the end of the file at the time)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             | P4 complete  | C1 zero-diff; `semantic_tokens.rs` gains module identity                                                                                          |
|                             | 5.1.2 Add `use super::*` or individual imports (the `include!` era implicitly inherited the scope)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     | 5.1.1        | `cargo build` is green                                                                                                                            |
| 5.2 Extract `refinement`    | 5.2.1 Move the refinement block (three non-contiguous regions in the original `checker.rs`; now the single file `checker/refinement.rs`, containing `ReturnRefinement` / `RefinedWalkCtx`), leaving the retained surface and 6 cross-boundary shared items in place                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    | 5.1.1        | C1 zero-diff                                                                                                                                      |
|                             | 5.2.2 Consolidate the refinement entry point as “`&self` + returns diagnostics,” **without leaving `impl`**: `collect_refined_binding_checks` (now `checker/refinement.rs`, `pub(super)`) no longer implicitly writes to the error channel through `&mut self`; the diagnostic set is returned to the caller, and the only write point is in the sole caller `check_module_impl` (`checker.rs`, located by symbol). **Rationale for not leaving `impl`**: this family’s field surface contains only `self.env` (leaving `impl` is technically feasible), but converting both the entry point and traversal to free functions would also move these call sites: `resolve_type_annotation` has 8 production sites (6 annotation paths + `refined_walk_stmt` + `collect_refined_var_names_in_stmt`), `collect_param_refinements` has 2 production sites + 1 test site, and this would create a reverse dependency from the retained surface (signature collection) to `refinement`—contrary to the coupling-reduction intent of this step | 5.2.1        | —                                                                                                                                                 |
| 5.3 Extract `annotations`   | 5.3.1 Move the 10-item annotation-validation family (now the single file `checker/annotations.rs`; `check_annotation_type_names` is the `pub(super)` entry point, the other 9 items are private to the family, and `is_predicate_head` is a free function within the family)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           | 5.2.2        | C1 zero-diff                                                                                                                                      |
|                             | 5.3.2 **`collect_used_in_type` (`pub(crate)`) remains `pub(crate)` and under the `checker` module path**: it is a **shared-surface** function (consumed by both `collect_function_signature` and `inference/statements.rs:16`), and 5.3.1 was measured **not to migrate it** ⇒ the “zero caller changes” criterion **was already satisfied**, so **do not add** a `pub(crate) use annotations::*;` re-export. **Constraint retained**: if it is migrated with the family in the future (into annotations or another later batch), `checker.rs` must add a `pub(crate) use annotations::*;` re-export so that the import remains unchanged                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              | 5.3.1        | **“Zero caller changes” is the hard acceptance criterion for this step: `git diff src/frontend/core/typecheck/inference/statements.rs` is empty** |

**Hard constraint**: `collect_used_in_type` is used across modules by `inference/statements.rs:16`.
**If** the function is migrated with the annotation family in the future, **then** `checker.rs` must
add a `pub(crate) use annotations::*;` re-export so that the import remains unchanged; 5.3 was
measured **not to migrate it**, so this batch did not add a re-export (the criterion was already
satisfied).

**Only split blocks that are proven to be large.** Do not split modules of only 200–400 lines—that
would increase navigation cost, reduce cohesion, and provide zero decoupling benefit. The remaining
submodules (signatures / type_defs / imports) are to be split if their files grow back to 1,500
lines.

**6.9 Model and Invariants (First-Principles Rewrite, 2026-11-13)**

> **Model**: D62’s end state is a **unified item world**—type positions and value positions share
> one set of compile-time items. One strength declaration produces one quantifier reading
> `q ∈ {0,1,ω}`; `q` is the **sole input** to slot allocation, and the call-site argument view and
> implementation-header binding view are two projections of the same fact. Equality is a **pure
> decision** (identical after normalizing both sides; does not bind type variables); evidence is the
> **sole entry point** for q=0 slots (four sources: literals/value environment/single-value
> pinning/Γ equalities); erasure is the **runtime consequence** of q=0 (holding for both closed
> terms and open/recursive terms); Σ’s construction sites **reuse** the same evidence interface
> rather than creating another one. **Completion criterion = invariants hold, not completion of
> subphase names.**

> **B.d prerequisite: decision-point protocol (not yet documented)**: RFC-027 §12.1 states that “a
> decision point first follows the unified path; after unified failure it may use equality, but must
> first roll back partial bindings produced by the unification attempt.” The implementation must
> answer: whether the entry point is an outer wrapper around `solver.unify` or a new `decide` layer;
> whether defeq is attempted only when both sides are ground (with no unbound variables); the
> snapshot/restoration boundary and cost; and whether unify and defeq share one budget or have
> separate budgets. **Responsibility boundary**: unify continues to handle subtype/Any/Never; defeq
> only decides equivalence and does not take over subtyping; bidirectional subtyping must not be
> treated as equivalence (RFC-027 §12.1). **Provide the protocol and production call graph before
> writing code**; 6.9.3c’s wiring contract was wasted over two rounds because it assumed
> `can_assign` was the decision point, while `AssignmentChecker` has zero production instances.

## Implementation Points: Dependencies and Parallelization

### Mandatory Serial Main Chain

`P0 → P1 → P2 → P3 → P3.5 → P4 → P5 → P6 → (P7 ∥ P8) → P9 → P10`

> **P3 stop-the-bleeding path (adjudicated 2026-10-05)**: P3’s prerequisites are narrowed to
> **2.3.2 + 2.4.1 + 2.4.3** (multi-file corpus layer + two red criteria). The rest of P2 (2.1 IR
> verifier, 2.2 snapshots, 2.3.1/2.3.3 differential testing and performance baseline) can proceed in
> parallel with P3. Stopping the bleeding from correctness vulnerabilities must not be blocked by
> criterion-infrastructure construction; however, **P4 must still wait for all of P2**—the unified
> Driver requires all three layers of criteria to be in place.

| Constraint                | Reason                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| ------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| P0 → P1                   | The three prohibitions constrain every P1 action (1.2.x adds `mod` declarations to `mod.rs`)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| P1 → P2                   | Reviving tests changes the test count and corpus baseline                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| P2 (after narrowing) → P3 | Vulnerability criteria must be **written as red first** (2.4.1/2.4.3), and the multi-file corpus layer (2.3.2) must exist so that the red tests have somewhere to run                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| P3 → P4                   | Fix bugs before refactoring; the reverse order would freeze bugs into the phase table as “established behavior”                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| P3.5 → P4                 | RFC-029g’s (#399) deletion surface covers the rewrite targets of P4 4.2.2 / P5 / P6 / P7 / P8 respectively (the list is in §P3.5 of this document)—reverse order means repeating the same deletions on the new grammar, new checker layout, and new IR (D56)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| P4 → P5                   | The `include!` refactor and checker split change the same file                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| P5 → P6                   | Consecutive changes to the same file must be separate; otherwise, regressions cannot be bisected                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| P6 → P7 / P8              | If type representations do not converge first, the new IR will grow into a third representation; **P7 gate = the A/B/C exits of 6.9** (I1–I3, I5, I7; namely, 6.9.2 including C3, 6.9.3 including d, and completion of 6.9.4), while D (Σ) does not block; P7 may consume only the quantifier-derived views and defeq interface and must not create a parallel ledger; the 7.0 pure-move batch is a P7 prerequisite, is not subject to this gate, and must not consume undecided defeq/quantifier interfaces |
| P7/P8 → P9                | The final form of 9.5’s snapshot baseline and 9.3’s `pub(crate)` leak count is taken only after P7/P8                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |

### Parallelization Groups

| Group                                    | Members                                                                            | Basis                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| ---------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| **A (the only group authorized by RFC)** | P7 ∥ P8                                                                            | Disjoint file sets: `ir.rs`/`ir_gen.rs`/`bytecode.rs`/`translator.rs` vs `lexer/*`/`parser/*`                                                                                                                                                                |
| B                                        | 1.2.1 ∥ 1.2.2 ∥ 1.2.3 ∥ 1.2.4                                                      | Each independently adds a `mod`; revert file by file                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| C                                        | 2.1 ∥ 2.2 ∥ 2.3.1 ∥ 2.3.2 ∥ 2.4                                                    | The three layers of criteria are mutually independent                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| D                                        | 4.4 (proof-layer cleanup) ∥ the entire P6 line                                     | `02` explicitly states in S5 that it “should proceed independently of S1-S4”                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| E                                        | 4.2.5 ∥ 4.2.6 ∥ 4.2.8                                                              | All are mutually independent after 4.1                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| F                                        | 9.3 ∥ 9.9 ∥ 9.10 (the three scripts introduced in P0 may be developed in parallel) | 9.5’s snapshot baseline must be taken last                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| G                                        | S3 ∥ S4 ∥ S5                                                                       | Disjoint file sets (verified on 2026-10-05: S3 changes `docs/src/dev/design/check/` + `config.js`; S4 changes `docs/src/rfc/` + the `check_tracking.py` generator; S5 changes two `pub` items in `src/frontend/core/typecheck/`; there are no intersections) |

**Cannot run in parallel (file overlap)**: P1(1.1.x) ∥ P8(8.0.x); 1.2.1 ∥ 8.3.2; 6.0 ∥ S2 (same
batch files for B6/E5); 4.3.2 ∥ 9.2 (now unified under P4); **3.4 ∥ P3.5** (`checker.rs` /
`environment.rs` are the same files—the external track’s `pub`-deletion batch and the silent-channel
fixes must be serial).

**New internal document constraints**: 6.0→6.1→6.2→6.3→6.4→6.5→6.6 is strictly serial; 7.0 →
7a→7b→7c→7d is strictly serial (7.0 is the pure-move batch preceding P7), and 7b’s `Phi` arm must
precede 7d.

## Key Decisions and Rationale

- **P0 is an independent phase rather than part of P9**—gates are “post-hoc checks,” while rules are
  “pre-hoc judgments.” P9’s scripts cannot prevent “patching what should be refactored”; only
  D0–D4’s review checklist can.
- **P9 is the sole authoritative CI-script inventory**—the original G3 gap’s three overlapping
  inventories made closure impossible. This table merges them, with 10 active scripts each owned by
  one phase (9.8 was cancelled by the user on 2026-11-24), making report-only status and hard-gate
  timing explicitly traceable.
- **P3.5 incorporates RFC-029g rather than leaving it as a “separate track to do after the
  refactor”**—its deletion surface overlaps with P4/P5/P6/P7/P8’s rewrite surfaces (RFC-039 D56).
  Deferring it until after the refactor means repeating the same deletions on the new grammar, new
  checker layout, and new IR; this is the same lesson as incorporating 7e’s `2315`/`2341` and S4’s
  RFC-status correction.
- **P5’s steps are supplied by this document rather than folded into P4**—P4 is already the largest
  single-point risk, and adding the checker split would exceed a revertible granularity.
- **5.3.2 uses “zero caller changes” as its hard acceptance criterion**—the split must be
  independently revertible.

## Known Limitations and Risks

- **1.3.x (fixing exposed defects) has no regression criteria**—it only says “the fixed defects must
  not be rolled back,” but lacks a record requirement identifying what was fixed. **Execution
  convention**: every 1.3.x fix commit message must reference the fixed test name and defect
  description as retrospective bisection evidence.
- ~~**7b.1 is too coarse**~~ **Fixed (2026-10-05)**: split into 7b.1a / 7b.1b as two exclusive
  commits per DoD 6.
- **8.2.1 is too coarse**—about 89 renamed references; missing one will **silently change
  associativity**.
- ~~**D17 / D20 have no corresponding Level 3 tasks**~~ **Fixed (2026-10-05)**: D17 landed as 7e.1,
  D20 landed as 4.5.1/4.5.2; D32/D34 opcode reclamation was incorporated into 7e.1, with deletion
  left to P10 S6.
- ~~**The `2315` / `2341` data-loss defects were originally separate issues**~~ **Fixed
  (2026-10-05)**: incorporated as 7e.2 / 7e.3. The exception table (throw/try) is core language
  semantics and must not be left as a later implementation item.
- ~~**E2 (`lib.rs:568/582` `todo!()`) has no phase ownership**~~ **Fixed (2026-10-05)**:
  incorporated into P10 S2.
- ~~**F7 (opcode-gate extractor) has ambiguous ownership**~~ **Fixed (2026-10-05)**: incorporated
  into P10 S6’s compile-time gate task.
